mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST < previous 12-month average) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 12M moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate increase above 4.6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous value AND UNRATE > 4.6% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which compresses earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12M moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL above 3% and FEDFUNDS above 4% for two consecutive months signals a dual shock of inflation and restrictive policy, which increases uncertainty and risk premiums, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS > 4% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive policy regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced marginal propensity to consume, which depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12M moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 while the unemployment rate simultaneously falls below 4% signals an overheating labor market, which raises wage inflation and increases recession risk, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between month-over-month growth in housing starts (HOUST) and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns, as new housing construction boosts materials and financial sector activity.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST month-over-month change and S&P 500 5-day forward returns falls below 0.3 or turns negative for any 12-month rolling window.
